articleTitle: E-CNN: ensembled CNN learning approach for pneumonia detection in chest X-ray images
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Pneumonia, a substantial global public health issue, is a pulmonary illness characterized by inflammation in the air sacs in either one or both lungs and can be triggered by several pathogens, such as bacteria, viruses, and fungi. In this regard, deep learning (DL) methods have demonstrated their effectiveness in classifying pneumonia which is a severe respiratory illness that specifically targets the lungs, particularly when analyzing chest X-ray (CXR) images. Therefore, significant efforts are being made to identify the source of the infection to assist clinicians in accurately diagnosing the etiology of the disease. The objective of this work is to investigate the efficacy of deep learning in the classification of pneumonia, utilizing transfer learning and the proposed weighted ensemble approach by utilizing a CXR dataset available publicly at the Kaggle repository comprising healthy and pneumonia cases caused by either viral or bacterial origins with a total of 5863 images. The preliminary results show our weighted ensemble approach stands out in performance achieving an accuracy of 98.40% significantly. The result demonstrates that current structures can accurately diagnose the sources of pneumonia and our deep CNN-based weighted ensemble learning approach could be a valuable tool in diagnosing upcoming unidentified diseases.

articleTitle: EconVisor: Indian economy forecasting application
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: EconVisor is an interactive time series analysis application designed to assist users in predicting Indian economic indicators such as GDP, sales, employment opportunities, and other relevant information. This prediction is tailored to the user’s selected industry type and desired future time frame. The application leverages time series analysis techniques to provide insights and forecasts specific to the Indian economic landscape, helping users make informed decisions based on anticipated economic trends within their chosen sector and timeframe. This tool provides valuable insights into the economic implications of different industries, supporting decision-makers in policy formulation, investment strategies, and resource allocation. In the research work, an extensive dataset of over 20 years’ time span is used. The dataset is integrated from 10 reputable organizations, including the National Association of Software and Services Companies (NASSCOM), the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), The World Bank, the Ministry of Tourism (MoT), the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), The Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance (IPA), the Annual Building Construction Cost Index from 1981 to 2022, the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG), the Government of India, and the Central Electricity Authority of India (CEA). In the proposed work, four statistical and Machine Learning (ML) models are applied such as Auto-regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest (RF), Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM), and simple Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). These models are chosen for their different strengths and capabilities, allowing users to select the most suitable model for their specific forecasting needs. The outcome shows that the RNN model performs better in comparison to other models.

articleTitle: Let them eat data
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to enhancing the farm-to-fork value network through comprehensive data integration. This initiative aims to leverage advanced data analytics and digital transformation techniques to address critical challenges in the food supply chain, including inefficiency, waste, and sustainability. We illustrate the potential for data-driven solutions in food manufacturing, distribution, and consumption. The paper explores the implications of data sharing for innovation and proposes a model for system monitoring and governance within the food industry.

articleTitle: Towards ethical AI: risk management and privacy in the age of innovation
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: This research paper addresses the alignment of ethical artificial intelligence (AI) development with data protection laws, focusing on the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the anticipated Artificial Intelligence Act. It highlights the importance of data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and fundamental rights impact assessments (FRIAs) in assessing AI-related risks, with the aim of protecting individual rights. The study assesses existing ethical frameworks and risk management systems, identifying their strengths and limitations. It advocates an integrated approach that combines DPIAs, FRIAs and ethical considerations to ensure that AI systems are developed and deployed responsibly.

articleTitle: Understanding new product development in digital startups
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The study performs an in-depth investigation of new product development (NPD) in digital startups. It is informed by process theory highlighting the sequence of stages in which NPD is advanced. Using a multiple-case study design, the study shows how common process models are implemented in digital startups and contextualized. Contrary to the prevailing view in the extant literature on NPD in startup companies, the findings demonstrate a high degree of completeness and quality of the NPD process in digital startups and purposive decision-making about deviations. Collecting best practices, the study makes recommendations for implementing NPD and lays the groundwork for better theory with important implications for today’s digital economy.

articleTitle: A fuzzy logic approach for dynamic trust evaluation in VANETs
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) are susceptible to security threats due to their dynamic and open nature. Trust management is a critical aspect of VANET security that enables vehicles to assess the trustworthiness of other vehicles and entities in the network. Traditional trust management systems use rigid threshold values to determine the trustworthiness of vehicles, which can lead to false positives and false negatives. To address this problem, we propose a trust management system for VANETs that uses fuzzy logic to determine the trustworthiness of vehicles. The proposed system uses fuzzy logic rules to calculate the trust level of a vehicle based on various factors such as its node nature, distance between nodes, time in network and interactions. We evaluate the performance of the proposed system using simulation experiments and compare it with a traditional threshold-based system. The results show that the fuzzy logic-based system outperforms the traditional system in terms of accuracy and false positive rate. The system also has the advantage of being adaptive and flexible, as the trust levels can be adjusted dynamically based on changing conditions in the network.

articleTitle: Detection of pulmonary embolism with improved Xception architecture
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The blocking of arteries in the lungs through blood clots is known as pulmonary embolism. This blood vessel block usually originates in the legs and travels to the lungs causing fatal damage. An imaging test called Computed Tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography scans the lungs for blood clots. The preferred method for identifying pulmonary embolism is CT pulmonary angiography. Manual examination by radiologists increases the workload, consumes more time and also requires experience for correct examination. The objective of this paper is to propose an improved Xception architecture based on Convolutional Neural Networks. The existing architecture is improvised by replacing the Relu activation function with the Swish activation function. This improves the feature extraction of the algorithm thereby improving efficiency in terms of loss and accuracy. The algorithm has been trained and tested using the standard RSNA-STR Pulmonary Embolism CT Dataset. It is evident from the experimental results that our model achieves an improvement of 3.4% and 1.4% in terms of accuracy and loss respectively.

articleTitle: Revitalising food supply networks through trustworthy data sources: an emergent toolkit for data sharing clubs
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The food system, and other similar opportunistic and dynamic supply systems, are increasingly exploiting digital data to increase operational efficiency and effectiveness. Digital data is plentiful and fluid but introduces challenges to security, privacy, trust overheads, and myriad others when sharing with services beyond traditional organisational boundaries. The focus of this paper is to explore the emergent tools and processes necessary to establish and sustainably cultivate a data-sharing structure that can serve the needs of a dynamic food and drink supply system or similar collaborative supply chain. We also address the role of the data sharing club as a structure that employs a customised governance framework for that unique structure. Central to this approach is the need to understand the interactions of people, technology and organisation.

articleTitle: Supply chain resilience: capacitated reliable fixed-charge facility location problems
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Supply chain resilience is predominantly intertwined with the design of the supply chain, and the crucial problem in this regard is to determine the location of facilities. Models for reliable facility locations address this resilience challenge by considering site-specific probabilities of unexpected failures and the potential need to reassign customers. In this paper, a novel capacitated version of the reliable fixed-charge facility location problem is addressed, where the failure probability of each facility is site-dependent, differing from the models in the literature. Facilities are assumed to have limited capacity for demand allocation, and the capacity of facilities can be increased to a predetermined value if any disruption occurs in the supply chain. To solve this problem, a nonlinear mixed-integer programming formulation is developed. The linear version of the proposed model is also presented. Since the problem is known as NP-hard (nondeterministic polynomial time), a novel Relax-and-Fix heuristic is developed to solve the problem. A number of experimental instances for different network sizes are solved to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. The obtained results show the efficiency of the proposed models and the proposed Relax-and-Fix heuristic.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of synthetic data vault (SDV) and privacy-preserving graphical models with latent variables (PRIVLAVA) in synthetic data generation for relational databases: an evaluation study
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Synthetic data generation has become a pivotal technique in overcoming the limitations posed by data privacy concerns and data scarcity in developing and testing data-driven applications. This study aims to compare two leading synthetic data generation tools, “Synthetic Data Vault” (SDV) and “Privacy-Preserving graphical models with latent variables” (PrivLava), focusing on relational databases. By evaluating their performance across various metrics, we seek to understand their strengths, weaknesses and best application contexts.

articleTitle: Socio-technological influence on trust in artificial intelligence in digital agriculture
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The paper investigates trust in artificial intelligence (AI) within socio-technological parameters to increase adoption of AI-based solutions in agriculture. Despite the benefits provided by AI-systems and the aforementioned trust factors, acceptance and adoption of AI-solutions have not been consistently observed, especially in agriculture. We employed qualitative research techniques conducting semi-structured interviews with experts from the agri-technology industry. Findings indicate variations in the level of trust in AI from one solution to another, depending on the design/appearance of the solution and how familiar it appears to farmers. Additionally, the importance of the social environment in building trust, particularly in circumstances of low general and technology knowledge, was highlighted. This research contributes to advancing our understanding of trust in artificial intelligence by providing insights from a social-technological perspective. On a practical level, the findings offer valuable insights to technology providers for designing and implementing their offerings.

articleTitle: Malware and botnet prevention in smart building IoT devices using blockchain-enabled federated learning
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The project proposes an AI-driven framework to enhance malware and botnet detection in smart buildings, employing blockchain and federated learning. It aims to overcome the limitations of conventional security methods by introducing a more dynamic and intelligent detection system. The initiative seeks to improve IoT security, establishing new standards for protecting smart building infrastructures against evolving cyber threats. Through the integration of blockchain and federated learning, the project addresses data security and privacy challenges, ensuring robust detection capabilities across various IoT environments.

articleTitle: Artificially intelligent regulation: global norms, international political economy and the Brussels effect
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The European Union (EU) has the largest global consumer market and is planning to formally adopt the so-called ‘AI Act’ (actually a regulation on AI) in mid-2024. That law is deeply embedded in the ‘digital acquis’, the series of laws passed by the EU institutions which include the Digital Markets Act and Digital Services Act of 2022. It is not possible to lift the AI Act wholesale into any other jurisdiction’s law, nor would that law survive being lost in such translation. The ‘Brussels Effect’ describes the adoption and adaption of European Union law in other nations, most famously the 2016 General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which came into force in 2018 and has been widely hailed as setting a global standard for data protection that other nations copied. The problem with that ‘Brussels Effect’ analysis is that it needs to be somewhat nuanced to be adapted to local norms – normative regulatory and corporate compliance behaviour. Many other nations did not adopt the EU's GDPR, but a separate law, the 2018 Convention 108+ of the Council of Europe, the 47-member human rights organisation founded in 1953 that predates the EU and has members including the UK and Turkey, though it expelled Russia in 2022. As a political scientist of cybersecurity and European legal technology expert, we assess the degree to which there could be an AI Act Brussels Effect. If such a ‘Brussels Effect’ in AI is unlikely or highly constrained, are there other external models that nations are using to inform and develop their own laws on AI? Both the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and UN Education Social and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) have agreed declarations of AI ethics principles, but these are non-binding norms, written as normative guides not laws, and thus not even soft law, let alone hard law that can be enforced. We conclude that global norms may be influenced by the Brussels Effect of the AI Act, but the degree to which this will happen will be dependent on how far alternative global/local models resonate and on the perceived need for corporate compliance at different levels.

articleTitle: Analysis of critical success factors for blockchain technology implementation in supply chain: a Delphi study
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Blockchain technology is expected to have a disruptive impact on supply chain management. To date practical implementations are fewer than expected and insights into the critical success factors (CSFs) of blockchain implementation are limited. This study couples a systematic literature review (SLR) with expert insights captured through a Delphi study to answer the following research questions: 1) What are the CSFs for implementing blockchain technology in the supply chain? 2) How do supply chain management practitioners perceive the CSFs in supply chains? 28 success factors have been identified by SLR. The Delphi study was employed test if these are necessary and sufficient, and prioritise them. This study provides a novel theoretical framework for the CSFs of blockchain technology adoption. This study assists decision-makers and policymakers in understanding each CSFs’ significance and devising the appropriate strategies and policies to address implementation challenges.

articleTitle: Improving CNN model training time efficiency using MPI-driven parallelization and ensemble learning
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have proven remarkably effective in various computer vision applications, such as object detection, image segmentation, medical imaging, and classifying handwritten numbers. On the other hand, CNN training on large datasets can be highly compute-intensive, resulting in lengthy training times. To address this problem, this paper proposes a novel method to reduce CNN training time for classification problems. To achieve this, we divide the training dataset across several CPU cores using Message Passing Interface (MPI) parallelization. Furthermore, we employ an ensemble learning method that combines the predictions of separate models trained on various subsets of the dataset using a majority voting scheme. We consider the MNIST dataset for the experiments. The results of our experiments show that, while retaining promising accuracy, the approach we propose significantly reduces the CNN model's training time up to 45.13% and 91.67% depending upon the machine specifications compared to the sequential approach.

articleTitle: Securing connected and autonomous vehicles: analysing attack methods, mitigation strategies, and the role of large language models
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) are revolutionising transportation, promising increased safety, efficiency, and convenience. However, their reliance on digital connectivity introduces new cybersecurity vulnerabilities. This paper comprehensively analyses various attack methods targeting CAVs. We discuss the potential consequences of these attacks and propose mitigation strategies to enhance CAV security. Furthermore, the paper explores the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) as a novel approach to fortifying CAV cybersecurity. Finally, we examine future challenges and opportunities within this rapidly developing field.

articleTitle: A comparative analysis of zero-shot rhetorical role classification in legal domain
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive analysis of multiple transformer architectures and their capacity towards rhetorical role detection in legal documents. Specifically, this research employs a zero-shot text classification mechanism. We experiment on a corpus comprising of fifty manually marked judgements from the Supreme Court of India. The models investigated in this paper include BERT, BART, DistilBART, DeBERTa, and RoBERTa. The overall objective is to find the most proficient model in categorizing sentences according to rhetorical roles. The findings presented in this paper indicate that DeBERTa exhibits superiority over its counterparts in terms of F1 metrics across the majority of the classes. This study also highlights the efficacy of advanced natural language processing (NLP) frameworks in automating the semantic dissection of legal documents.

articleTitle: Privacy-preserving personalised federated learning financial fraud detection
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Financial institutions increasingly utilise AI-based applications to enhance fraud detection. However, in today's highly interconnected world with higher access to information and technology, fraudulent activities are also becoming increasingly sophisticated. Thus, models trained only on local historical data may struggle to identify such complex transactions effectively. To address this challenge, the institutions may share their data with each other. However, such data sharing activity is constrained by regulatory compliance and institutional trust requirements. We propose adopting Federated Learning (FL) with Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PET) as a state-of-the-art solution to bolster fraud detection capabilities while addressing concerns related to data privacy and competition. Financial institutions face the dual mandate of improving fraud prevention and maintaining the security and privacy of customer transaction data. FL offers a path to achieve these goals by enabling collaborative model training across multiple financial organisations without the necessity of sharing sensitive transaction details.

articleTitle: Towards green and sustainable artificial intelligence: quantifying the energy footprint of logistic regression and decision tree algorithms
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) significantly impacts the advancement in numerous application domains such as healthcare, education, energy systems, transportation, entertainment, weather forecasting, and finance. However, the exponential increase in the use and adoption of AI algorithms, particularly Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, has raised serious concerns about their environmental impact due to their higher computational demand. In the literature, most of the research in AI has focused on increasing the performance of the algorithms without considering their effects on energy consumption. In this context, this research aims to address the need to quantify the energy footprint of machine learning algorithms to pave the way towards green and sustainable AI. This paper conducted an experimental study on the energy consumption of two state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms – logistic regression and decision tree while applying them to a popular benchmark Iris dataset. The energy consumption is quantified and compared through thorough measurement and analysis. The findings of this research contribute to the ongoing efforts to enable eco-conscious and sustainable AI applications and systems. The paper source code is available online on Github1 .

articleTitle: Edge markets for the usage of data and digital assets: the Dataswyft data wallet
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: This paper reports on the creation of the Dataswyft Data Wallet Technology – a technology that could coordinate the market for data computation and usage at the edge. It argues that the failure of centralised systems to unlock the value of data can be resolved by relocating its usage and portability to the edge. The paper reports on the work to create 3 edge markets for discoverability, validation and transfers and present the findings. The findings propose that a market coordinating intermediary, a data wallet, is necessary to emerge the edge market. The paper concludes with the transformation potential for firms to enter edge markets and policy implications.

articleTitle: Understanding online posts from social media using large language models and topic modelling: challenges faced by women in African farming
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: We describe a novel methodology combining social media listening (SML) and natural language processing (NLP) to examine women's involvement and the challenges they face in livestock and poultry production in Sub-Saharan Africa. Specifically, we explore women's roles, their perspectives and attitudes regarding disease prevention, treatment, vaccination and diagnostics in ruminant and poultry farming. Pulsar Platform™ was used to scrape social media data from X platform (Twitter), blogs, forums and Facebook using specifically designed Boolean search expressions. Large language models (LLMs) were used to filter and classify relevant posts. Audience profiling was conducted using Pulsar Platform™. Using a combination of a LLM and topic modelling we identified key themes in the data, which were subsequently summarised into narratives by a LLM. The findings were organised into four major themes regarding women’s roles in livestock and farming, challenges for women farmers, perspectives on disease management and control, and the value of training, education and animal health interventions for women and households in the region. Overall, this methodology demonstrated how SML data and NLP methods can successfully filter and analyse data from social media to provide pertinent real-world insights.

articleTitle: Precision healthcare analytics: a machine learning approach for efficient length of stay estimation in acute malnutrition patients in Mali
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Estimating “Recovered length of stay” is useful in the better utilization of resources, effective planning treatment and cost-effectiveness in managing acute malnutrition patients. This study proposes a machine learning approach to improve the precision in estimating “Recovered length of stay” for patients suffering from acute malnutrition. The present work analyzes the seven Machine Learning (ML) models to estimate the recovered length of stay. The best two models were chosen based on the standard evaluation metrics such as MSE (Mean Squared Error), Coefficient of determination (R2), MAE (Mean Absolute Error), MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error). Further, the input features to the best two models are reduced using one of the commonly used dimensionality reduction algorithms known as Principal Component analysis (PCA). The proposed approach is fully tested using the particular dataset for acute malnutrition cases and estimates the recovered periods for the patients. The results of the experimental tests show that the use of multiple regression models, especially Decision Tree (DT) and Support Vector Regression (SVR), results in the greatest improvements in the estimation of in case of acute malnutrition. In addition, the models presented a R-squared value of 0.9459 and 0.9316, and they are the best models to capture the complex features of patient recovery times.

articleTitle: Trustless is not trust free: how to build trust for organisations adoption of blockchain technology
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: This study investigates the antecedents and targets of trust influencing organisations’ decisions to adopt blockchain technology. Through a grounded theory approach involving 20 semi-structured interviews with executives and managers from 19 enterprises in China, we identify six key trust antecedents: authoritarian culture, perceptions of feasibility, successful precedents, evaluation of organisational trustworthiness, data governance, and leadership engagement. These antecedents influence adoption decisions through three targets of trust: the technology itself, technology providers, and participants. Notably, data governance and external forces such as industry and national leadership engagement exert a pervasive impact across all three targets within an authoritarian context. A holistic conceptual framework is developed to elucidate how these trust antecedents impact trust targets, thereby shaping decisions regarding blockchain adoption. Furthermore, we discuss how these targets of trust influence adoption decisions, considering diverse perceptions of their functions and importance, as well as their interrelationship as complements or substitutes in the decision-making process.

articleTitle: Awakening the Web of self-sovereign data with ESPRESSO: a scoping review of Solid’s and Dataswyft's readiness for decentralized private search
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The Internet in 2024 has become a mechanism for turning users into suppliers of data to third parties, a disappointing descent from the noble origins of the World Wide Web. Human-generated data becomes fodder for artificial intelligence to devalue human intelligence at scale. To take back control, one approach is for “self-sovereign” users to store personal data in servers of their own, and let third parties come to them for access, which the data owner grants selectively and granularly. This is the private, decentralized, re-idealized Web. Solid provides a manifesto, a solution, and a protocol for this re-idealization. Before Solid came Dataswyft's Hub-of-All-Things, a personal data ecosystem with a similar philosophy of self-sovereignty, developed from the perspective of exchange of personal metadata as an economic asset. However, barriers to adoption of private personal online data stores threaten the survival of these systems. The original World Wide Web was globally adopted because the power of search made it irresistibly useful in everyday life. The ESPRESSO project is developing ways to infuse the private, decentralized Web with the same power. In this scoping review we investigate the search-readiness of Solid and of Hub-of-All-Things using the ESPRESSO framework.

articleTitle: A robotaxi artificial intelligence safety failure
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Full self-driving capability in autonomous vehicles within all operational domains is one smart mobility vision companies compete to achieve. They view self-driving as aiding transportation efficiency and enabling the commercialisation of ”robotaxi” services and other use cases. However, the testing of robotaxis within urban areas continues to see safety-related incidents. We provide a case study of a 2023 San Francisco event to illustrate why the behaviour of Automated Driving Systems is under scrutiny. A serious injury to a pedestrian by a robotaxi occurred and the subsequent mishandling of the regulatory reporting requirements saw further investigations. This resulted in suspended commercial operations, job losses, and a vehicle recall. We construct a timeline of the incident and the follow-up events. Subsequent third-party analysis of the incident provides further insights and raises a typical dichotomy of safety versus commercial considerations. We use the insights to argue for governments and regulators to consider a different approach to developing and testing self-driving capability within public spaces, namely, the collective engineering of one universally verified self-driving artificial intelligence usable by all vehicle manufacturers.

articleTitle: Utilizing the potential of AI to Revolutionize talent management in contemporary organizations
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to an umbrella of technologies, from machine translation and chatbots to self-learning algorithms and self-driving cars. Individuals using these technologies gain a better understanding of their surroundings and make informed decisions, while organizations increasingly turn to AI innovations as ways to adapt or disrupt ecosystems while strengthening strategic and competitive positions. AI achieves its full potential by streamlining existing operations, improving automation, data utilization and transformative capabilities - it outperforms at tasks such as recognising patterns, making predictions and interfacing with humans thereby realising its full potential. Thus, our research findings highlight the numerous advantages AI brings to organizations. AI improves performance across various dimensions such as finance, marketing, and administration while simultaneously increasing process efficiency resulting in enhanced outcomes and simplified operations. Also, it holds great promise for improving talent management strategies through sophisticated workforce management systems. This study seeks to outline the necessary conditions for creating an AI-powered solution capable of effectively meeting talent management challenges. Research in this area centers around creating an intelligent Human Resource Management (HRM) automation tool with a talent intelligence module as its cornerstone, with the primary goal of optimizing integration between professional assessment and planning features. A design science methodology and structured machine learning techniques serve as cornerstones of this comprehensive AI solution framework. Additionally, the proposed framework is enhanced by merging insights from Digital Transformation Triad (DTT) theory and Dissemination of Innovation (DOI). This combination provides a robust strategy for effectively addressing AI-related challenges. Moving beyond automation aspects of talent management solutions, this research offers practical recommendations to researchers so that their approaches meet organizational-specific talent growth requirements. Ultimately, this research investigates AI's transformative potential within talent management while outlining a holistic strategy to use AI for workforce planning and professional assessment within contemporary business environments.

articleTitle: A new encoding of implied volatility surfaces for their synthetic generation
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: In financial terms, an implied volatility surface can be described by its term structure, its skewness and its overall volatility level. We use a PCA variational auto-encoder model to perfectly represent these descriptors into a latent space of three dimensions. Our new encoding brings significant benefits for synthetic surface generation, in that (i) scenario generation is more interpretable; (ii) volatility extrapolation achieves better accuracy; and, (iii) we propose a solution to infer implied volatility surfaces of a stock from an index to which it belongs directly by modelling their relationship on the latent space of the encoding. All these applications, and the latter in particular, have the potential to improve the risk management of financial derivatives whenever data is scarce.

articleTitle: Genetic ledger – pioneering secure and authentic data storage through DNA and blockchain
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: The rapid increase in digital data necessitates advanced storage solutions. This paper introduces the DNA-chain system, an innovative integration of DNA data storage and blockchain technology. Our hybrid system utilizes the high-density storage capability of synthetic DNA to handle massive amounts of data, alongside blockchain’s robust security and traceability features. We detail techniques for encoding digital data into DNA sequences, addressing compression, redundancy, and error correction. Multi-layered encoding organizes data efficiently, while Optimized Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) processes facilitate swift data replication and retrieval. Live-Data Mutation Checks ensure data integrity against natural alterations, and Self-evolving Blockchain technology continuously adapts to new security challenges, enhancing protection against tampering. The system leverages DNA’s parallel processing abilities, enabling multiple simultaneous data accesses, which improves throughput. DNA Digital Twins and Genetic Smart Markers mimic natural redundancy, enhancing retrieval efficiency. Real-time genetic analysis provides instant insights from stored data, supporting applications like long-term archival and time capsules. The DNA-chain system combines biological science with cryptographic techniques, offering a revolutionary, secure, and efficient data storage paradigm suited for future challenges.

articleTitle: Understanding the financial control and management of advanced service contracts
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive analysis of financial strategies and controls essential for managing advanced service contracts effectively. It explores cost understanding, emphasising the significance of accurate cost estimation and adopting different pricing models to maintain profitability and competitive advantage. The paper considers using different revenue models, highlighting the shift towards service-oriented offerings and the challenges in revenue recognition, compliance, and cash flow management. It underscores the importance of aligning financial management practices with advanced services, including adherence to evolving international accounting standards and risk management to ensure financial stability and regulatory compliance.

articleTitle: CGRec: a convolutional graph neural network-based recommendation model for social networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on AI and the Digital Economy (CADE 2024)
abstract: As social network platforms persist to attain widespread popularity, the volume of content generated by user, and other online community data is experiencing rapid growth. Recommender systems are gaining popularity due to its capability to filter out large chunks of data and deliver more specific personalized behaviour by its ability to utilize side information and user interaction which makes it ideal for recommending choices based on user. GNN are being used in social recommender system since it works better with graph data and representation learning. The graph data is represented via item-user graph and social user-user graph. The central approach for representation of graph is the learning latent factors of users rating. Developing a social recommendation system with GNN aspects some challenges like social graph relations have Heterogenous strengths, item-user graph embeds both opinions and interactions, user is tangled in two main graphs i.e., user-item graph and social user-user graph. To deal with three challenges parallelly findings have proposed a convolutional graph recommender system (CGRec) model. In this, a systematic method is presented for simultaneously incorporating communications and opinions within the item- user graph. This network model effectively models two distinct graphs with varying strengths. Rigorous experiments conducted on two physical-world datasets confirm the efficacy of the CGRec model.
